quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a single line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line is best for normal riding. However, when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway, riders should form a single line.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They limit how far you can see to the sides.
They let you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some riders worry that helmets limit their vision. This is not true. Approved helmets allow riders to see everything they need to see for safe riding.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle into a turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the turn.
questions.explanation: To lean into a turn, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this may make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How should you apply the brakes when stopping?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: How do you get the shortest stopping distance in a straight line?

options.text: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Do not lock either brake.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes if a hazard occurs.
It makes it easier to communicate with the other rider.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes if a hazard occurs.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. Doing so limits your escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Why should group riders avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not leave enough space to maneuver.
Riders on the left cannot exit the highway easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not leave enough space to maneuver.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should never ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough room to move and avoid hazards.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride on the left side of your lane. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with low traction, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than normal.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use caution and apply the brakes gently.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a clear view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. Avoid staying in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: For a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine if you feel sleepy.
Wear warm clothes to protect from wind and cold.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear warm clothes to protect from wind and cold.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Limit riding to 6 hours per day and take rest breaks every 2 hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants, as they cause extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes occur on trips shorter than 5 miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you are riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave to get the driver's attention.
Slow down and move out of the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and move out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, speed up quickly or slow down and drop back to get out of it.

questions.question: If you use a sidecar to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Secure the load so it doesn't shift.
Place the load loosely in the seat.
Secure the load at the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it doesn't shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they don't shift and affect handling. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Is designed to handle corners at any speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a motorcycle with a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: Shoes that don't cover the ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use low heels to prevent catching on foot pegs. Leather or durable gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve grip on the controls.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen the most?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green are best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should NOT:

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges—these are slippery.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Why is it good to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrower view so you can focus better.
You will have more time to react to other drivers' moves.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to other drivers' moves.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.
